record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Does there exist a countable complete lattice L whose Scott space Sigma L=(L, sigma(L)) is non-sober? Here sigma(L) is the Scott topology on the order L, and non-sober means that some irreducible closed subset of Sigma L is not the closure of a unique point.

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. ([32]) Is there a countable complete lattice that has a non-sober Scott topology?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(L,\le)$ be a complete lattice, i.e., a partially ordered set in which every subset has a supremum and an infimum. A subset $D\subseteq L$ is directed if it is nonempty and every pair of elements of $D$ has an upper bound in $D$. A subset $U\subseteq L$ is Scott open if (i) $U$ is an upper set ($x\in U$ and $x\le y$ imply $y\in U$), and (ii) for every directed set $D\subseteq L$ with $\sup D\in U$, one has $D\cap U\neq\emptyset$. The collection $\sigma(L)$ of Scott open sets is a topology on $L$, and the resulting space $\Sigma L=(L,\sigma(L))$ is called the Scott space of $L$.

A topological space $X$ is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$ (a closed set $A$ that is not the union of two proper closed subsets) is the closure $\overline{\{x\}}$ of a unique point $x\in X$. Otherwise $X$ is non-sober.

Question: Does there exist a countable complete lattice $L$ such that the Scott space $\Sigma L=(L,\sigma(L))$ is non-sober?
artifact.category_tag: Sobriety of Scott topologies on complete lattices
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by Miao, Xi, Li, and Zhao in a 2022 preprint "Not every countable complete lattice is sober" (arXiv:2205.00250), who constructed a countable complete lattice whose Scott space is non-sober. A subsequent paper strengthened this to a countable complete distributive lattice.

status_evidence.title: Not every countable complete lattice is sober
status_evidence.snippet: We construct a countable complete lattice whose Scott space is non-sober, answering an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: A countable complete lattice with non-sober Scott space exists, resolving the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Not every countable complete distributive lattice is sober
status_evidence.snippet: Mathematical Structures in Computer Science article showing a countable complete distributive lattice with non-sober Scott topology.
status_evidence.claim: Strengthened result: even a countable complete distributive lattice can have non-sober Scott topology.
